notes: Read SKILL.md in full (single-file skill). The skill covers NFS server install and /etc/exports, exportfs, firewall rules for NFS, client mounts and /etc/fstab, autofs, server/client performance tuning, Kubernetes NFS PV/PVC and the NFS CSI driver.

Medium: following it has the agent run root-level system changes — apt/dnf package installs, systemctl enable/restart, editing /etc/exports, /etc/fstab and autofs maps, mount/umount, writing /proc/fs/nfsd tunables and sysctl, adding ufw/firewalld allow rules scoped to 10.0.0.0/24, and `helm install` of the NFS CSI driver into kube-system. Acceptable because these are the standard, user-requested steps for setting up NFS on the user's own hosts; firewall changes only add narrowly scoped allow rules, and nothing disables a security control or deletes data beyond the throughput test file it creates (SKILL.md:272-274).

Review before applying: several sample exports use no_root_squash (SKILL.md:56, 70) and /shared is exported read-only to all hosts (SKILL.md:59); the table itself warns 'use cautiously'. The CSI driver Helm repo URL tracks the master branch (SKILL.md:315) and is unpinned. Related skills (linux-administration, block-storage, performance-tuning, backup-recovery, object-storage) are named as optional reading only.
